newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbian authorities shut down town's radios, TV.
newsitem.headline: Serbian authorities shut down town's radios, TV.

text.p: Serbian authorities have closed down six small private radio stations and a television channel in the southern Serbian town of Kraljevo, independent media in Belgrade said on Monday.

Independent B92 radio said inspectors of the federal Telecommunications Ministry began the process against the stations, which carried mostly local news on limited facilities, on Friday and finished on Sunday.
"People in Kraljevo will be able to receive only state media programmes in the future," the radio said.
Police accompanied the teams which confiscated the broadcasters' equipment, the radio said.

The independent newspaper Nasa Borba reported that the inspectors banned all stations in Kraljevo apart from M-radio which has an operating licence and which supports the ruling Socialist Party of Serbia, the paper said.
Kraljevo is ruled by the Serbian opposition but control of the press falls under Socialist-ruled republican jurisdiction. The stations closed were close to the opposition.
The West has repeatedly warned Serbian authorities against cracking down on independent media.
The United States insists the improvement of relations between Washington and Belgrade depends also on improvement of press freedom in Serbia.
Serbian authorities argue that many private broadcasters do not have an operating licence.
Media control is vital to the ruling Socialists ahead of Serbian presidential and parliamentary elections due to be held this autumn.
